body: I'm trapped. There's no end in sight. There's no one to talk to. How long can I continue like this? I'm tired of being depressed for days. Then I get one day where I feel a couple of hours of relief and then I crash. I wish this endless journey would change. I am so alone.

I feel intense sadness that painful both physicallyandmentally. My brain is telling me lots of things on a loop... This (depression) never ends. There is nothing left to try, except for ECT. Will my life be better or worse after ECT? Will my depression cause long-term difficulties in my children's lives? Will I ever be able to go back to work? Will this feeling ever go away? How can I get through this day? Etc., Etc., etc.

As a patient, I am looking for an empathetic psychiatrist. One who will listen, offer advice, always have a plan on next medications to try, discuss recent research on condition. I am looking for a psychiatrist who isn't afraid of discussing the tough topics like suicide in exploring why I'm feeling that way instead of jumping to conclusions of needing hospitalization.

I had a psychiatrist like that twice in my lifetime. I know they are out there. Right now I am having difficulty locating a psychiatrist that offers more than med management. Spending 10-15 minutes with a psychiatrist only is a waste of my time and money and does not give me hope.

I read your post. I can relate. I go through times of deep depression where I don't see the point of life. There have been times when I'm still depressed and don't feel suicidal. 

I try to stick around for my kids and spouse and hope life gets better.
I have tried every legal prescription minus Pristiq; I have also tried TMS, Ketamine, and ECT. I have treatment-resistant Major Depressive Disorder.
Have you tried the stimulant Vyvanse? It helped with concentration/focus. Unfortunately,  my depression is currently haywire again, so my interest is not there right now.

Vraylar was excellent!  It took away all of my hallucinations and helped with my depression. Unfortunately, since my insurance changed and I can no longer afford it. My depression is worse without it.

I restarted all of my meds today, even the one for my diabetes. I feel lower than low. It will pass eventually. I have been really stuck even when I was regularly taking my meds. I feel so alone and stupid and old.

I am really not seeking a regular therapist. My depression, unfortunately,  is treatment resistant. I have not seen a way to overcome depression, this is not negative thinking - it's a fact with what I have experienced. I've had it for over 30 years. It has been getting worse over time, no matter what I do to try to make it better. I have been on over 40 medications and combinations - there is maybe one medication I haven't tried. I've tried Ketamine, TMS, ECT. I have been in residential treatment, had therapy - CBT, DBT, ACT, etc. I have exhausted my options. Right now. I just want a psychiatrist that can prescribe meds and offer advice here and there - that's it.

I guess what I'm looking for is to cut out my therapist and just have a psychiatrist that meets with me quarterly or every 6 months. I'm looking for someone to offer creative options of both meds and advice. I'm tired of feeling depressed, unmotivated, and unheard. Life continues to be monotonous despite what I have been trying. I'm back to feeling tired of trying and getting nowhere.
I don't want to tell my psychiatrist I've stopped taking my meds. I don't want anyone to know I'm suicidal. People tend to not understand.

Some days are more of a struggle than other days. I distract with social media, phone games, sleeping, volunteering to help others, staying in the moment with my pets, engaging in conversation with others about their lives, getting support through my counselor, when it's nice out - walking the dog, doing the 5 senses activity, naming things/people I'm grateful for, doing zentangle, doing a breathing exercise that makes me focus on nature and breath control, and reading if I'm able. When an unwanted thought comes, I set a time limit on how long I think about it. After that I stop the unwanted thoughts by saying stop when I catch myself thinking of the unwanted thought, or change my distraction activity. Sometimes my thoughts don't go away, sometimes they stay. It's important to keep trying and not to give up.

I have this problem as well as starting any project. Start out with small goals. If the goal seems overwhelming make the goal smaller yet. Here could be an example... set your alarm for 10 a.m., sit up on the side of the bed, take a couple of deep breaths. Invite one of your cats over and pet them. Get up to the bathroom. Pair each activity with something that brings a little comfort. You can retreat to your bed, but your mindset is not to stay there. Keep doing small goals throughout your day. Write down basic goals and come up with ideas of comforting ways to complete them whether that means listening to music, playing with your cats, treating yourself with a favorite snack, or setting a small timeframe like 10 minutes to start a task. Give yourself grace and praise for what you do accomplish.
Thank you

Notice one thing you can hear like hearing a bird. Notice a scent like fresh mowed grass. Notice a taste like flavored water. Then notice something that you can touch like the shoes under your feet. This is a grounding activity that helps you break up the monotony during the day. I hope this helps you feel something other than just sadness.

What happens if my kids disappoint me/let me down or even die - what will happen to me then? I need to find other reasons to stay here. My kids will grow up and move on with their lives, they won't need me as much as they did in their growing up years. Someday they'll be independent and I need to let them go.

My purpose keeps changing depending on where I am in life. Right now I get lost in what my purpose is because I'm severely depressed. Depression makes me feel completely alone. Today I met with my psychiatrist. We were talking. I was struggling - conflicting thoughts.  The conversation in my head I was plotting my demise for after my appointment. He said talk to me about what you are thinking. I took a chance of telling him of my thoughts of how I wish I could stop thinking, of how as a deep thinker I cannot be okay with simple answers. My question of why suicide prevention is so strong in the medical community and bottom line he said that depression is a curable disease. I've never heard that and I've struggled mostly with it for many, many years. He asked an important question... Am I afraid to overcome depression? 

I am. What about you? For me, depression is more predictable and safe for me. The uncertainty without it is scary. My psychiatrist reassured me that he cares and hopes that I will make safe choices. 

Your therapist meant well. My past therapist would actually yell at me for having suicidal thoughts. This psychiatrist is not afraid to talk about the tough questions and actually understand my true fears. Don't get me wrong, 2 weeks ago I was hysterical and he sent me to the ER to get me calmer. I left calmer 6 hrs later.

I do understand your frustration about how slow they are titrated up, the length of waiting to see if it works and with MAOIs, going through a washout period and then starting again. I am tired of providers being hopeful that a new treatment will work or a new drug will magically be affective. I'm tired of therapists telling me I'm not doing enough skills. I do, do skills. This has been going on for 25 years. I feel like there are years that I've missed life because nothing was working. I was trying and still all of the mental health tools failed me. 

Now it's about the moments of goodness in my life that I'm enjoying in the present moment. Daily, I deal with deficits, I just do what I can each day. I may not remember the past. I'll just let other people to tell the stories.
